# Cntxt Labs

> Cntxt Labs (also written cntxt, pronounced "context") is a software company based in New Zealand, founded by Cristian Rus and operating since 2017. It designs and builds apps for iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch, along with software for the web and Android. The products cover time and attention, health and fitness, food safety and the outdoors, and have been downloaded more than 1.75 million times.

This is the complete text of https://cntxtlabs.co, written for language models and agents. Every page is here, so there is no need to crawl the site to answer a question about it. A shorter index is at https://cntxtlabs.co/llms.txt. Quoting is welcome; please name Cntxt Labs and link to https://cntxtlabs.co.

Last updated: 2026-10-12

## Company

- Name: Cntxt Labs
- Short name: cntxt, pronounced "context"
- Type: privately held software company
- Country: New Zealand
- New Zealand Business Number (NZBN): 9429053827906
- Operating since: 2017
- Founder: Cristian Rus, https://cristianrus.me
- Website: https://cntxtlabs.co
- Email: info@cntxtlabs.co, the only address the company uses
- App Store developer page: https://apps.apple.com/us/developer/cristian-rus/id1778834894

Cntxt Labs is a design-focused company, specialised in building software products and services across Apple platforms, web and Android. For over a decade the work has focused on how design and technology influence the way people behave, and on turning that into software people continue to use. The product themes cover time and attention, health and fitness, and the outdoors.

## Contact

The best way to reach Cntxt Labs is to email info@cntxtlabs.co. It is the only address the company uses, it is read every day, and it goes directly to the people who build the apps rather than to a support desk.

For help with an app, write to the same address and say which app it is. The version of iOS, the device, and a short description of what happened will usually identify the problem on the first reply. Bug reports and feature requests are welcome, and a good number of the features currently shipping started as an email from somebody using the app.

Press enquiries, review copies, promotional codes, partnership proposals and anything else commercial go to the same address. Requests from journalists and reviewers are answered as a priority.

## Products

### Left

Left shows the time you have left. The year, the month, the week, the day, the hour, the minute and your life, drawn as symbols that dim as they pass.

Habits can run daily, several times a day, weekly, or to a schedule you set. Streaks are there to protect, aims count anything you can build up or cut down, and a habit or a streak can be shared with a friend. Dates that matter sit ahead as countdowns, each with its own list of things to get done, imported from the calendar if wanted.

The planner puts that next to the rest of the day: Apple Calendar, Reminders, the weather, sleep and workouts, in one view. A fasting tracker, a focus timer and a mood log sit in the same place, so the day is planned where it is spent.

Left is used by more than 1.5 million people around the world.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/left
- Website: https://getleft.app
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/left-widgets-for-time-left/id6740155884
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch
- Privacy policy: https://getleft.app/privacy

### SafePlate

SafePlate replaces the paper diary in a New Zealand kitchen. Fridge temperatures, deliveries, cooking and cooling checks, cleaning, training and sickness records are made when the work happens, kept for four years, and ready for a verifier visit.

It runs on the web, Android and iPhone. One subscription covers the whole team. Records save on the phone first if the kitchen is offline, then upload when the signal returns.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/safeplate
- Website: https://safeplate.nz
- Platforms: web, Android, iPhone
- Enquiries: info@cntxtlabs.co

### KiwiCamping & AussieCamps

Two camping apps built the same way, each for one country. KiwiCamping is for New Zealand: more than 6,500 DOC campsites, huts, freedom camping areas, holiday parks and dump stations. AussieCamps is for Australia: more than 74,000 campsites, caravan parks, national park sites and rest areas.

In both, the whole directory is stored on the device, so a place still opens after the last bar of reception, which is when it tends to matter. Search and filter by facilities, price and access, save places into collections, and turn a shortlist into a trip with routes, distances, dates, notes and to-dos.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/camping

#### KiwiCamping

KiwiCamping is a camping map and road-trip planner for New Zealand. More than 6,500 places (DOC campsites, huts, freedom camping areas, holiday parks, dump stations and practical stops) are stored on the device, so they still open where there is no signal.

Search and filter by facilities, price and access, save places into collections, and turn a shortlist into a trip with routes, distances, dates, notes and to-dos. Weather, alerts and directions sit on each place; guides cover how DOC sites, huts and freedom camping actually work.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/kiwicamping
- Website: https://campingapp.nz
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/camping-map-nz-kiwicamping/id6746952595
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad

#### AussieCamps

AussieCamps is a camping map and road-trip planner for Australia. More than 74,000 places (campsites, caravan parks, national park sites, rest areas and useful stops) are stored on the device, so they still open where there is no signal.

Search and filter by facilities, fees and access, save places into collections, and turn a shortlist into a trip with routes, distances, dates, notes and to-dos. Weather, alerts and directions sit on each place.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/aussiecamps
- Website: https://aussiecamps.app
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6801098680
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad

### txtpod

txtpod converts articles, links and PDFs into narrated podcast episodes. Save something once, and listen to it wherever you already listen.

Episodes are read by more than thirty natural voices across over twenty languages, with translation available. They are delivered to a private feed that works in Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Overcast, Pocket Casts and any other player that supports RSS.

txtpod also generates episodes on chosen topics and a daily brief on the subjects you follow, with custom artwork, listening streaks, a synchronised web app, and integrations with Instapaper, Matter and Readwise.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/txtpod
- Website: https://txtpod.app
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/txtpod-articles-to-podcast/id6748379680
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad, web
- Privacy policy: https://txtpod.app/privacy

### NoSnus

NoSnus builds a plan to get you pouch-free, with a date on the calendar rather than a vague intention to cut back. Answer a few questions about your habit, and it sets the path around the way you actually use pouches.

Every pouch is logged. Cravings are handled in the moment they arrive, money not spent is counted as it adds up, and a bad day does not undo the work. It is made for nicotine pouches and snus, and for nothing else.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/nosnus
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/quit-zyn-velo-snus-nosnus/id6791343296
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad

### Other iOS apps

More apps on the App Store, for health and everyday habits. They are small, focused tools rather than a single suite, each built around one job and meant to stay out of the way. All of them run on iPhone, and none of them require an account to start using.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/ios

#### ftnss

ftnss is a private AI coach over Apple Health. It can see training, nutrition and sleep from the apps already in use, including Apple Watch, Strava, Garmin and MyFitnessPal, and you can ask it about any of it.

It builds plans across strength, endurance, mobility and recovery, logs meals from a photo or a description, and adjusts as the week actually goes. HRV, VO2 Max, sleep and training load are read from Apple Health, so it knows when to push and when to recover.

Progress is presented through dashboards for weight, energy and performance, alongside more than fifteen cards covering workouts, steps, sleep and longer term trends.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/ftnss
- Website: https://ftnss.app
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ai-health-insights-ftnss/id6742253667
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch
- Privacy policy: https://ftnss.app/privacy

#### Bites

Bites logs a meal from a sentence. Describe what you ate, and Apple Intelligence returns the calories and macros. No scanning, no measuring, and no food database to search.

It synchronises with Apple Health, tracks a daily calorie goal, and shows the energy remaining once activity has been counted. Frequent meals can be saved so the next log is a tap.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/bites
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/meal-tracker-bites/id6755179382
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad

#### NotSoBusy

NotSoBusy turns a day or a week into a picture of when you are busy, without sharing your calendar. It reads Apple Calendar, Google Calendar and Outlook, and draws each event as a block of time: no names, no titles, no details.

Share the image in a message or an email. There is no account and no login, and no data leaves the device.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/notsobusy
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/share-schedule-notsobusy/id6745011162
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad

## Privacy

Left, txtpod and ftnss each publish their own policy: https://getleft.app/privacy, https://txtpod.app/privacy and https://ftnss.app/privacy. ftnss sends some anonymised data to an AI model to produce plans and insights; identifiers are removed first.

KiwiCamping, AussieCamps, Bites, NoSnus and NotSoBusy share this policy:

The app runs on the device. There is no account to create, and no personal data is collected or stored. Purchases are handled by RevenueCat, which retains only what is required to verify a purchase and restore it if the app is reinstalled. Google services are used for crash reporting, anonymous usage statistics and certain features within the app. None of it identifies the user, and none of it is sold or shared.

SafePlate is a subscription for kitchen teams and works differently: records are uploaded rather than kept only on the device. The policy above does not describe it. Ask info@cntxtlabs.co for details.

## Common questions

- Who makes these apps? Cntxt Labs, a software company in New Zealand, founded by Cristian Rus.
- How is the name said? "Context". It is written cntxt.
- How do I get support? Email info@cntxtlabs.co and say which app it is.
- Do the apps cost money? They are free to download. Some have paid features, handled through the App Store and RevenueCat. SafePlate is a subscription that covers a whole team.
- Which platforms? iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch. SafePlate also runs on the web and Android, and txtpod has a web app.
- Is there an Android version? SafePlate runs on Android. The other apps are made for Apple platforms.
- Do the apps need an account? KiwiCamping, AussieCamps, Bites, NoSnus and NotSoBusy do not. Check each policy for the others.
- Is Cntxt Labs available for client work? Write to info@cntxtlabs.co about working together.
